question: How do Promises and async/await work? How do you handle errors?

scenes.sub: A promise is a value that arrives later.
scenes.say: Promises and async await. The interviewer wants three things: the states, how errors flow, and when to run things in parallel.

scenes.head: Think of a pizza order
scenes.say: Think of ordering a pizza. You get a buzzer and you go sit down. You do not stand at the counter. Later the buzzer goes off, and either your pizza arrives, or they tell you they sold out. A promise is that buzzer. Await means: sit down until it buzzes.

scenes.head: A promise has three states
scenes.say: A promise starts pending. It later settles exactly once, either fulfilled with a value, or rejected with an error. After that it never changes. Then callbacks and await receive that result.

scenes.head: Errors: try and catch
scenes.say: Await pauses the function until the promise settles, and a rejection becomes a normal throw. So try and catch just works. One trap: fetch only rejects on network failure. A four hundred or five hundred response still resolves, so you must check res dot ok yourself. Then the catch block handles both.

scenes.head: Sequential vs parallel
scenes.say: Two awaits in a row run one after the other, so two hundred milliseconds here. If the calls are independent, start both and wait together with promise dot all. About one hundred milliseconds. If any promise rejects, promise dot all rejects immediately. When you want every result regardless, use all settled. It reports fulfilled or rejected for each one.

scenes.head: In the interview
rows: Promises chain and share one error path, no callback pyramid.
No. It pauses only that function. Other code keeps running.
It rejects as soon as one rejects.
Forgetting await, or awaiting in a loop that could be parallel.
scenes.say: Likely follow-ups. Promise versus callback? Promises chain and share one error path, so no callback pyramid. Does await block? No, it pauses only that function. If promise dot all fails? It rejects as soon as one rejects. The common mistake: forgetting await, or awaiting in a loop that could run in parallel.

lines: Pending, then fulfilled or rejected, exactly once.
await turns a rejection into a throw. Use try and catch. Check res.ok.

scenes.say: Pending, then fulfilled or rejected, exactly once. Await turns a rejection into a throw, so use try and catch, and check res dot ok with fetch. For independent work, use promise dot all. When you want every result, use all settled.
